items.title: Lillian Hardin Armstrong Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: So, I went over with the band, and, I asked for the music. So, Eddie Garland was the one who called the numbers, and Lawrence Dewey was the one who used to knock them off, you see.

ctx.x: that's true, no, I was watching, I was watching the volume meter, oh, I see, mm-hmm, I watched the volume meter occasionally,

so, well, I imagine about the, after I'd been there about a month, this band from New Orleans came in the store one day, and this woman booked musicians and singers, in different cabarets, and, and, dance halls, too, so, they came in there, to see this woman about getting a job for her, and that was this band from New Orleans, with Eddie Garland, Roy Palmer, Lawrence Dewey, Sugar Johnny, and, who's playing drums? Tubby Hall, I guess.
I was going to say one of the hall boys.
Sugar Johnny, Louie Kepard on the guitar, Roy Palmer, Herbert Lindsay, Eddie Garland, and Toby Hall on the drums.
he beat me up there with his band, his orchestra. What do you mean by he beat you? Would you tell him? His orchestra was up there before mine was. Ah-ha. Do you know any of the
things that they played at that time? I do not know, but I did that. My piano player came to

Chicago with him, Lil. Lil was his name? Lil Hardin, Lil Armstrong's first player. Uh-huh. Lil Hardin, Louis Armstrong's first ride. Mr. Dewey, we'd like to know the various combinations of instruments that played, uh, for the various, uh, occasions that you people were hired in New Orleans. Would you tell us how many there were and generally what instruments played? Seven. Seven pieces.
